newsitem.title: USA: Trials of Ribi melonoma vaccine to start.
newsitem.headline: Trials of Ribi melonoma vaccine to start.

text.p: Ribi ImmunoChem Research Inc said patient enrollment has been completed in a Phase III study of its its Melacine vaccine for early-stage melanoma patients.

The study is being sponsored by the National Cancer Institute and conducted by the Southwest Oncology Group. It will involve 689 patients and will determine the ability of Melacine to prevent the recurrence of melanoma in Stage II melanoma patients who have had primary tumors surgically removed.
Ribi said an interim analysis is scheduled for the fourth quarter of 1997 and the final analysis will be in 1998.
The company said there are about 47,000 Stage II melanoma patients in the United States. Historically 30 percent of Stage II melanoma patients have recurrent disease within five years.

Ribi also said it is preparing a New Drug Submission for Melacine seeking commercial approval in Canada for therapy of late-stage melanoma, which it plans to submit in the first quarter of 1997. It also plans regulatory filings seeking approval for use in late-stage patients in the United States and Europe in 1997.

An earlier Phase III study of the vaccine showed it produced "esentially equivalent survival" to an aggressive experimental four-drug chemotherapy regimen that is the standard treatment for late-stage melanoma.
